name: Stormwarden Gao
title: Keeper of Cloudroot
description: A spare, grey-haired woman in waxed travelling robes. A long iron-bound staff leans at her shoulder; a small bronze compass sways at her hip though the needle keeps no north up here. Her eyes are the colour of clean rain.
dialogue: Hold a moment, cultivator. I do not refuse the road — I only weigh who walks it.
Up past the terraces, the ridge has become a place of crossings. Storm-crows nest where they should not. A Heavenly Sword disciple was seen on the pass last month; he did not come down.
Before I open the pass, bring me proof that you have not come here only to die. A storm-crow's feather, say. Survive the ridge, and we will speak of the peak.
The Sky-Spire is not a mountain you climb. It is a mountain that climbs you. Forget this, and every step is your last.

2: You carry Baixu's warranty now. The pass is yours; I only hold the door for you.
-2: I know your face from the courier's notes. Do not mistake the cloud for a hiding-place.

name: Ghost of Patriarch Mingshu
title: Last of the Jadestep
description: The translucent shape of a tall man in a crane-and-peak robe, his beard still un-combed four centuries after his death. He does not quite stand on the stone; the wind passes through his sleeves without lifting them. When he turns to face you, the flagstones beneath show no shadow at all.
dialogue: Nineteen of us stood here the morning the tiger came. I — was the twentieth. Had I stood with my disciples, there might have been twenty.
The beast is not a beast. It is a hunger with four eyes. The sect thought it could bind the hunger. We were wrong by exactly one student.

If you would close what we left open, bring me the fang of the thing that ate my hall. I cannot rest until it is set on the last stone here. Then, and only then, will I teach what I could not teach in life.
Do not pity me. Pity the student who drew the tenth scar on the Skyweaver's wall — and did not live to finish it.

companion_reply.blood_sworn_jin: Ah. A Pavilion shadow on my stones, and you — the thief's hunter, and the thief's mourner both. My disciples were less complicated. Be quick on my terrace; I do not wish to see another grey-robed man weep here.
companion_reply.disciple_meilin: A crane-disciple, here at last. The Sect of the Azure Cloud and the Jadestep were friends once, in the reign of the Third Emperor. Go carefully; the terrace still remembers being friendly.
companion_reply.venomhand_bai: A venom-handler on the terrace. Good — the valley's palms are honest, even when the hands are not. Do not touch the tenth scar in the Cloister wall; it is not finished, and it would not like you.

name: The Old Dog of Jadestep
title: Last Teacher of a Dead Sect
description: A thin old man with a grin that seems to belong to a younger face. He wears a patched grey robe with one unmended tear over the heart. He is pouring tea for someone who is not there — and when he looks up, he pours a second cup for you without asking.
dialogue: Sit, sit. The cushion is older than your grandfather's grandfather; it will not mind one more bony youngster.
They call me 'Old Dog' because I outlived everyone with a prettier name. When you live long enough, cultivator, fashion forgives you.
The nine scars on the wall were my students, each a senior brother to the next. The tenth I could not finish. Finish it for me, if you have wind enough in your chest.
Footwork before the sword, breath before the footwork, stillness before the breath. Try it tomorrow; you will be worse. Try it again; you will be worse still. On the fortieth day, be surprised.

companion_reply.blood_sworn_jin: Ha. A red-sleeve and a wanderer in my cloister. Sit, Jin — I pour tea for any man who is tired of the sect that made him. I have had many such students. Few of them lived. Drink slowly.
companion_reply.disciple_meilin: A crane still walking. Tell Baixu the old dog sends his respect, and that the terrace has not yet forgiven him for outliving me. He will laugh; he laughed the last time. Laughter is the Azure Cloud's one reliable swordstroke.
